sentences.text: This meeting is being recorded.
Hi, Andy.
Hey, how you doing?
Yeah, how are you?
Yeah.
Nice to meet you.
Yeah, nice to meet you too.
Apologies, I'm just trying to close loads of windows.
That's okay.
Whereabouts you base?
You're in Leicester, is it?
Yes.
So we're based in Midland.
Based in Leicester.
We've been here for about.
We've been around for about 12 years.
12, 13 years now.
So.
Yeah.
Well, it sounds.
What about to you?
Well, I live in Somerset.
Okay.
But we are based in.
In London.
Right.
Preference to work at home, but back to London.
Okay.
Yeah, it's, it's.
It's the way of working now, isn't it?
People enjoy the kind of hybrid working.
Whereas, yeah, too many years of spending five days in the office.
So I'm.
I'm kind of enjoying that myself.
Yeah.
I don't know how we did it.
It's strange, isn't it?
I used to have like an office in Shoreditch.
Like 30 staff coming in every day.
I can't imagine 30 kids in their 20s turning up for work.
It's hard enough.
Yeah.
People in their 30s and 40s.
Yeah.
I have two days in the office and three days at home and.
Yeah, I wouldn't have you any other way now.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
I've got a client in LA and I went in to see them.
Amazing office.
They've got like a helicopter landing pad on the roof and all sorts.
Really big agency.
But there was literally maybe like four or five people in this huge building.
It's huge.
It was.
It actually kind of doubled as an art gallery as well, but just nobody was coming in.
It was insane.
It was just like all this.
All death.
It's crazy.
It's just.
In all honesty, I think the productivity is actually really good, working from home, you know, because you don't spend that time in travel and then get exhausted and all the rest of it.
So, yeah, we.
Yeah, we do like it.
So, yeah, yeah.
Well, Leicester is.
Is a place I've visited a few times.
I don't know it hugely well, but that's definitely Midlands way, isn't it?
What's famous in Leicester?
Yeah, East Midlands, apart from our football team and of course the.
And the National.
We have the National Space center here.
It's a small place.
I mean, I'm.
I'm actually originally from London myself, so I was born and brought up in southeast London.
Oh, really?
And moved here about 17 years ago.
I used to run a.
A business previous to this and then whilst I was here, I sold that business in 2008 and then started up inside consultancy from there.
So we've been going ever since.
But yeah, less, less, less is a small place.
It's compared to obviously compared to London but you know the closest large city to us is Birmingham but huge.
Like we're only 40 miles apart but it feels as though it's the, you know, the kind of barrier from East Midlands to West Midland is huge.
Yeah, well, we're the same Bristol.
We never go to Bristol.
We prefer Bath.
It's more peaceful and quiet.
Yeah, yeah.
With it we're the same.
No, I totally get it.
It's probably a nice, easy, peaceful life in comparison to running around in cold, dark, dangerous London.
So.
Yeah.

So well, thank you for getting in touch and obviously always interested to see a.co.uk because we, we do work in America probably about 95 of the time so it's nice to see a business from the UK looking to list.

But yeah, I mean I can tell you a little bit about us first and then be good to learn more about you and what it is you're trying to achieve and hopefully we can, we can help you achieve whatever that goal is.
Sounds good.
So.
So we're a capital A Capital A group's an M and a advisory specializing in marketing services.
So our, our clients are usually all marketing agencies or investors into that space.
So it could be private investors or private equity firms and we work with them both buy buy and sell side.
We have the agencies co platform for sellers looking for buyers and we work on the buy side as well.
So we get to see deals on both sides of the table which is really insightful.
For the, the last 12 months or so we've probably done about 50 million in deals.
Like I said, a lot of that in the U.S.
yeah.
Anyway, it's growing.
We're probably about eight years old and my background is, is marketing services and media.
So I've come from your side of the table, sold my business and ended up over here.
So when did you sell?
Sorry?
When did you sell?
Okay.
Yeah, it was nice.
Yeah, it was long enough ago to, to feel like it was pain free almost.
Yeah.
Yeah good.
Okay.
Yeah.
We could learn more about you.
What, what are.
Yeah, well give me the background.
What, what are you doing?
So we're, we're, we're a very, very, very small marketing agency.
So we've been around for about 12, 14 years as I say and we primarily are based around website design, maintenance, hosting and build.
So currently we host over 150 websites on a nice retainer basis.
And on top of that, we do, we used to do organic social media advertising, but we stopped doing that and now we focus on paid advertising for.
On Google Ad on, on social media.
Are you there?
I am, yes.
Yeah, yeah, it's my satellite dish.
Sorry.
Okay, cool.
So, yeah, we've, we've, we've grown year on year.
We, you know, we have a headcount of about 13, 14 people.

It's solely myself and my wife who started a company and we are, I, I wouldn't say we're, we're niched in any way, but you know, we, we have, you know, just because of my background, we have, we have a few niches that we go into, one being the legal sector.
So most of our clients are, you know, sort of B2B professional services.
But we do have some additional niches with some Islamic charities, which is a very difficult market but a very lucrative market to get into.
So that's kind of our, our, you know, you know, one of our niches.
And in terms of why we want to sell.
So it's not, it's, it's not a distressed sale.
It's not something that we need to do very quickly.
You know, I've, I kind of have a figure in mind.
I have, you know, if we don't sell it, you know, in the next year or two or three, it, you know, it's not going to be, it's not going to be too bad.
But if we cancel earlier, it'll be better.
And one of the reasons is, is because, you know, we've kind of grown organically over the last few years and we have a year on year growth of about 10, 15, 20%, which is, which is very nice.
We're healthy, we've got reserves, we've got everything that we need.
But really what I wanted to do, this is going back a couple of years now, Andy.
I wanted to, to kind of acquire, to sell.

So I was looking for small agencies and I think the mistake I made was I approached them directly and you know, with the, with the idea of getting a deal done very, very quickly, you know, with a, with a much, much smaller agency than ours, we, we pitched for two and we lost both of them.
And it was just because they felt that, I mean, one of them actually said that came too easily.
So it was, that was an interesting thing.
So my background, you'll probably gather, is I'm not a designer, I'm not a developer.
So I, I come from a corporate finance background.
So you Know, I, I, you know, I, I kind of, I guess what I do is the old fashioned way of writing checks.
So I, I basically just pay the bills in terms of the actual doing the design work and the development work.
I have a very strong team behind me that does all of that.
So.
Yeah, and that's, that's basically it really.
And yes, that's the reason why we, we kind of look into sell.
Okay, brilliant.
All right, so just in terms of numbers then, have you got just that it can be ballpark for now, but just top line revenue and bottom line.
If I, if I show you, I have actually prepared something for you.
I mean, look, you know, when it comes to kind of the figures and I think that's probably one of our biggest strengths.
So if I show you what I've got, if you've got a few minutes, yes, we've got a really healthy retainer income.
Where are we?
There we go.
Yeah.
Okay, so I'm just going to share my screen with you.
So this is kind of our retainer income that, that we have.

So if we go to the dashboard you can see that kind of, you know, we, we have a, we have a retainer income for about 400,000 and we normally sell around about the sort of 10,000 pound mark every month.
So you know, we're kind of looking at an income of about 600,000, which is of course a very, very small micro company.
But kind of our EBITDA if you like, is about between 120 and 140,000.
So we, although we're very small, we're very profitable.
And if you look at our kind of, you know, the, the retainer income that kind of keeps us going and some every single month.
So you know, we, we have a, we have a very healthy kind of retainer income from a large number of clients.
So it's not as though we're dependent on one or the other, you know, so if we were to lose any of our clients, it really doesn't have a huge impact.
We've always had a very nice spread of income over a large number of small clients.
And what we have to do for that is very small because it's mainly retainer based hosting agreements that we have with them and all of them are under contractual agreements and so on and so forth.
So you know, we have a kind of retainer income for about 70, between 65 and 70% of our income.
Of the stuff that you're hosting, is there like a platform that you tend to work with more often?
I mean, are you on WordPress or what's the system?
Yeah, we only do WordPress.
So we only do WordPress.
We have a couple of sites and the clients are not leaving us.
They just say, look, we want you to manage it.
Sorry, you've got them for life, those types of.
Indeed we have, indeed, yeah.
And we, I think we got a couple of sites on Shopify that we just look after really.
But yeah, I would say, you know, 100% of our sites are WordPress.
Okay, so what is it you're looking to do?
You're looking to sell.
You were talking about sell through acquisition, but that's, that's off the table now.
You've, you've not, not necessarily.
So we have reserves off around about kind of the 200 mark, give or take.

And we wanted to spend some of that money in either buying a kind of a small building where, you know, we could rent some of it out, keep some of it for ourselves and kind of just grow the business, or we wanted to spend that on an acquisition for a smaller agency.
We wanted to get past the million pound mark, you know, so we thought, look, you know, if we buy a couple of agencies, you know, we can probably get, you know, rather than organically growing.
We can, we can grow through acquisition.
It still is on the table if we could find a suitable agency for us.

But equally if we feel that, you know, just to hit that million pound mark, we'll have to wait, you know, a longer time or it's more hassle than what it's worth, then we're quite happy to sell as well.
We're open to both.
Andy.

Yeah, well, seller, I mean it's possible to, to buy something for that price, but the problem is that these companies will be so small that it wouldn't take much to upset them and you would lose your money.
So, you know, as you know, agency businesses are people businesses, they're service businesses and people businesses.
So they're usually low multiples.
So let's just say a tiny agency that was worth 400k and you would give them 200 in advance and some kind of payout based on whatever it was churning out the back end.

So for 400k it could possibly be 100k EBITDA business and so it could be 400k of, of revenue that you could bought on the top which would, you're 100 right, would put you in the million pound mark and would make you more valuable than you are because it's a surer but for the buyer, but for that to Go wrong would only take one or two small things.
You know, when, when an agency is that small, 400, just imagine they're doing 400k in revenue, is probably half the size of you.
Six people, maybe even less than that.
Four freelancers, five freelancers, one guy that's running it, that person may take your turn to K and disappear.
You might fall out of them or whatever.
And I mean, you can.
When businesses are this more, you can sometimes just buy the, the book, you know, the book of clients and go from there.
But it's just finding those and finding, you know, because you're in, you're in Leicester, which is great because you're in the center of the universe.
There's, you know, you could have a north where you could buy something in Manchester, you could buy something in London.
Wouldn't really matter, would it?
Because it'd be just the same time to get there.
Or you.
Or Birmingham, which would make sense.
So I think that is definitely a doable goal.
But again, 10 agencies doing that.
You'd have to have 10 conversations.
You've got to close one of those and it could take you a couple of years.
Could take you a year to have 10, 10 serious conversations, make 10 offers and actually get one closed.
Statistically, that's kind of what you're looking at and it's just such a pain.
I don't know whether it would benefit you any more than just cashing out that 200 grand.

I mean, I, I'm a big believer in buying businesses, but I just think because it's so small, the risk is that somebody just ends up being an idiot and you just don't, you don't, you just didn't know that they were going to be like that and you just lose the 200k.
So it's just a bit of a tricky one because you've got to do the volume to find a good seller.
So you've got to meet a lot of people, kiss a lot of frogs, we like to say, to see if you can get there, like, you know what I'm talking about.
Because you, you come from that background, so you know exactly what it is.

I'm not saying it's impossible and it might be that you've got a network of like, you know, load of people that, that you can have those conversations with and we could certainly have them on your behalf, but we're going to cost money.
So we, we would charge £4,000amonth to go out and do that work for you.
So it's just chipping away at your, your pot of money.
So I reckon it's probably worth reaching out to people within your network.
But I think what you have is quite interesting anyway, so.
Because you're just so.
So the thing is with agencies is that there's millions of agencies every, you know, everybody's mum's got one.
It's just so easy to start an agency.
There's very little differentiate differentiation in the market.
But the first thing is you've got a legal sector niche, which is great.
So basically when you're looking for buyers, you want to be able to show them something that they can buy.
Now there are large agencies that are in that niche.
So saying, here's, you know, geographically different agency, you know, say we talk to a London based agency, we say we've got an agency in Leicester that does legal for them.
They might go, that's amazing because we want to get into the Birmingham market.
You've got a few clients in Birmingham that really works.
And then the other thing is the Islamic charities.
So obviously you're a business, an Islamic aligned business and that gives us another niche to go after as well.
So there's two, there's two things that very clearly differentiate you from the rest of the market, which makes just a really easy sellable business.
What are you going to get for it?
So I don't know what the 120k is yet, whether that's what you take your profits out of, because obviously we need to hire somebody like you to run the business after we bought it.

Again, a smaller business might mean that there is an operator in the market that just won't just have to be in the Midlands maybe, or, or you can easily move where it's HQ and everybody's off, you know, online anyway, so.
So you're probably going to get a 4x for it.
I would say.
Officially most valuations would come in at three, three and a half because of the, the size of the business.
But realistically people just don't sell 3x so buyers have to stump up for.

So it's worth about half a million, I would say, plus your 200k that you could take out if that wasn't running costs that's in that cash net was purely money that is tucked away then Potentially you've got 700k worth of cash waiting there.
Is that.
Yeah.
Sound like something that you're looking to do or what are you?
Yeah, yeah, kind of.
I mean I was, I was thinking, I was thinking about between 7 to, to 1 million is what I was thinking and I kind of done it at a, at a multiple based on, I mean maybe this was unrealistic.
I did a multiple based on seven.
I also did a net present value calculation and an adjusted ebitda so you know, taking away my salary.
So EBITDA is, is a great tool as you know, but adjusted EBITDA where you know, you might add a little bit it.
The multiple I got from a can't remember where it was Pitchbook I think it was.
So the multiple, look, you know, if I walked away with seven, I would not complain.
That's not, that's not something I would say.
And in terms of the niches, I mean the niche is absolutely fine.
I mean, you know, it, there's such a spread, Andy, that you know, even if we were to lose one or two of those clients, it wouldn't really affect the cash flow but the growth potential is huge.
So you know, you're kind of ballpark there.
Between seven and one is what I, what I would have gone for.
I don't think you're going to get 7x.
It's just purely the size of the business.
So you've got to think about this as risk for a buyer.
If somebody is buying at 7x, they're basically saying I'm going to pay this off over the next seven years using the profits from the business.
So basically I'm not profitable for seven years.
Right.
But again, going back to what I was talking about with other small agencies, the, the chances of this business falling over it is fairly high.
I mean you have shown that actually it's not with your client base that's brilliant and it's probably much more solid than most agencies.
It may even give it an extra 1x.
But the risk is always small with small businesses.
When you've got a business that's doing 10 million, to take that business out takes a lot of mistakes.
So from a buyer's point of view, the risk just isn't worth seven years of no profit before they get to a profit margin.
So it just is, it just is less.
I find that most agency owners, even though officially, you know, you would.
And when I say officially, I'm talking about what a bank would lend, a buyer would be about around three and a half x.
Right.
And they would look at how you can service that debt over a five year period.
Like I say, I don't think most sellers want to sell three and a half.
It just is not significant.
When you've got a small business, it's like I might as well just run it myself and do that.
So, so it tends to become a bit of a process of, you know, you've got to buy it for forex if you want it.
I think the legal thing and maybe the Islamic thing may it gets you into niches and gets you into some people, but I don't know how that, how far that would push up.

What I would say is we could list a price that you're comfortable with and I think is realistic because obviously we've got to put effort into listing it, but that's, you know, that's a balancing act and then we've got to find a buyer that's willing to part with the cash.
Now if you said, well, I would only list at 5, most of my team would probably say, yeah, it's dreaming, he's not going to get five.
But you just don't know.
So would I be happy with a five?
I would be comfortable with going at five as long as you're comfortable accepting three and a half because at the end of the day it's only worth what somebody's going to offer for it.
So.
Yeah, yeah, I mean, we, we've got to be realistic on it also.
What, what, how does it work?
What are your listing fees or what are your, how, how do your fuel fees come into this?
Yeah, so it's completely free to, to list on agencies.
We take 5% on deals that are worth over a million and 10 on deals that are worth less than a million.
We do have some supplementary costs if you want to engage us with anything else.
We have a complete M and a process and that would mean my team working every single day until we get it sold, which is 25,000 company your size, I would suggest.
Wouldn't want to spend that type of money.
Probably isn't, probably isn't worth it.
But we do take our fee, our win fees, net of whatever retainers you've paid.
So if we ended up earning 50 grand, you'd only as 25 on the, the day of the exchange or whatever.
But we also charge, and this is often the difficulty with small businesses, but again, you're in, you're from this background more than I am, so.
But we also charge 5k fee to prep a business to sell.
So we'll go through your books, we'll look at all the adjusted EBITDA stuff, we'll pull out things that we think are fair and get to a as good a price as we can get to.
And we're making a story really for the potential buyer of, you know, this is what Enzo's.
It, it would cost to replace him.
So we would make that adjustment and we would get to a price that we could argue the toss on based on that.
So like a 4 and a half, let's say for argument's sake we did 4 and a half X an adjusted EBITDA of 200k and then we would be close to your number.
I think my team would be happy with that as a, a realistic target.
And then we list, it goes out to our mailing list.
We have traffic on the site as well that we would pick up and I guess we would probably do.
I mean we normally charge for this but I think like I say, because it was like I said at the start, because it's in the uk it makes it a little bit easier.

But we'd probably do a quick search as well outside of that with one of our analysts who would come up with a bunch of buyers as well that we, you know, that maybe were off grid, that weren't part of our normal mailing list and we'd send it out, we'd send the teaser out and we'd see what, what came back in.
So it's very little risk to you in terms of cost.
There's none.
Unless you want us to do the.
Sorry.
We charge the money to get all of your materials together but if you are from an investment banking background, then it's just preparing evaluation and I am.
Which you might feel happy to do yourself.
So.
Yeah, I mean it depends, depends on what you're looking to do.
But I would say that probably the best route is if you don't have the time to do the prep that you.
We just do the prep and take it to market.
It would take about three or four weeks to get you up and selling and into one, one on one meetings with buyers.
And in terms of your experience in selling businesses, my side, the micro businesses, you know, in your experience, how long averagely does it take to, from market to, to at least interest.
Yeah.
So it's immediate as soon as it goes out our mailing list.
So we sold, we sold an agency probably about half the size of yours in LA.
We got 45 signed NDAs within 24 hours.
We had five offers and we closed with one of those.
It took us about two months to close off, an initial month of talking, so three months.
So you seem like a really knowledgeable guy and I think, I think we can work together and I, and I think we, we are, we are.
You know, I'm going to speak to my Wife, but we are probably going to go with you.
Do you honestly think that, I mean, in terms of, you know, look, I'm at the age now where my, my kids are kind of thrown in there, so I haven't got any overheads.
You know, I've got a couple of properties that we've got.
Is it worth me buying a business to get it past that million pound mark?
And I'm, I'm, you know, I'm gonna do, I'm gonna do something else after this business.
I'm 52 years old, I'm gonna do something else.
I, I don't mind spending another couple of years in it.

Do you think it's worth me just tipping it over that million pound mark and, and just going for it or, you know, and the other thing is also, would there be like, what about if I said to the buyer that I don't mind staying in the business as an md, for instance, for a couple of years, would that increase the price a little bit?
Yeah.
Could I get to that million pound mark a little bit?
I mean, I don't want to make a promise that we, we can't keep.
Would it get too many more?
I don't know.
We'd need to look into your books.
I do think 7 is too, is too rich a multiple.
If we can, if we can get your ebitdar up to 200, 250, then yeah, of course we can easily get you to that valuation.
Again, you are still a small business.
Even with a massive margin.
It doesn't necessarily, you know, negate all of the risk that comes with a small business because a 600k revenue business can fluctuate by 2 or 300 grand.
You know, I've seen businesses fluctuate by much more than that, so.
But you've got a really stable business with you in the business.
Yeah, of course it could be worth more.

And it's, it's actually, I think you've got a really interesting type of agency that's very solid and it's, it's, it's quite rare because you've got the hosting side of it and you're just building people's sites and just keeping them for clients forever.

So I actually, we work for, on the buy side with a WordPress guy and what he was doing was knocking on the doors of agencies like yours and just buying them all based on the fact that he can host their websites forever.
And he bought about 40 and he came to us and we found him like another 20 agencies in a couple of months.
He just had too many that he could buy.
So that was his business model.
Now to answer your question, I'm 52 this year as well.
So I know that you've, you're probably full of energy and you have at least another good 10, 20 years in you.
So it would, would I advise you to sell it?
It depends what you want to get into.

You know, it could be that you could take, you know, nearly a million quid out and invest it into property and it's just much more stable or what could you build an empire based on what you've got already?
And the answer is yes.
I mean you could, you could definitely do that if you were, if you were not too risk averse as well.
And you could actually, you know, leverage the target businesses that you're going after.

You could easily find a business that's the same size or bigger, you know, get a bit of debt and put it against, you know, particularly if it's a solid business like this where you've got repeat revenue and buy, buy for three or four multiples and then once you are up well over a million, that multiple does go up, you know, five, six.
So that multiple arbitrage from buying at three, three and a half and selling at five, six, seven is, yeah, is a really realistic thing to do.
So me personally, I would go for that option, but I'm an idiot.
So, um, but you know, my wife would say no, sell it and just let's go and buy, you know, a holiday home or something.
So I mean it really does depend.
I think the ball is in your court.
I would say if you've got the stomach for it, I would, I would buy.

If you got the stomach for the risk, I would buy a couple more businesses and bolt it on because it seems to me that you are really stable and I've just spoke to this absolute nutcase about an hour and a half ago.
These revenues like that all over the place, you know, complete creative and batshit crazy.
But it seems to me that you have that stable hand that will be able to build a business over a period of time through, through mergers and acquisitions.
And it 100 makes sense to me to do, to do that.
So if you've got the balls for it, I would say that that would be the one.
Yeah.
But it is the best conversation I've had with anyone so far and I've spoken to a lot of people.
I honestly, honestly really appreciate that.
Honestly, your valuation is kind of spot on as well.
I think, I think that's what I was expecting.
My wife thinks we're going to get 20 million for it.
You know, I said kind of, you know, it's, it's not that kind of business, but I think it's, it's kind of spawn.

I think I've got a conversation to have and if you can give me till Monday, I'll have a think about it, sleep over it, speak to my wife about it as well over the weekend and come back to you with an answer on which direction we want to go.
Yeah.
And so just, just to, to reiterate your fee.
So not you don't have a listing fee, but you have a kind of a set up for your 5,000 only.
If you want, if you want us to do the work, but if you want to create the IM for yourself, which is basically the deck that we sent to buyers when they signed an NDA.
If you want to create and I can give you a template, then that's, that's fine.
If you pay us to do it, we, we will put that together and we'll also do a full valuation and, and work with you on the, on the EBITDAR and the, the pricing on that.
So.
Yeah.
Whether you want to come up with your own price and deck or whether you want us to do it.
Yeah, the information memorandum, I think it might be worthwhile that we, we to it because I spoke to my, the only person who knows about it is my office manager.
She's on board with it and she, between herself and I, we're quite happy to stay in the business as well.
That's something that I'll come to at a later stage.
And she said that we can put the information memorandum together ourselves to save us, but we might, we might need you on certain things.
So you know, I'm gonna, I'm gonna think that it's going to be a, a fee to, to have that and then it's a 10 fee on sale, which is, which, which is absolutely fine.
Okay.
All right.
I think I've brought the information I need.
Yeah.
So I will, I will come back to you by Monday next week or on Monday next week and then we'll, we'll take the next steps from there.
Okay.
Perfect.
Perfect.
Amazing.
Thank you so much for your time and appreciate that.
Yeah, no worries.
I'll still do that in an email as well.
So you've got it.
And then yeah, happy to, to sort of go with whatever you want and if you need support on, on the buy side or you just want some advice, then yeah, we're here so.
Sounds good.
Amazing.
Thank you very much.
All right.
Nice to meet you.
Yeah, likewise.
Speak soon.
